answer: Across a planning horizon, irrigation agents serving a meadow below a mesa get spending limits through trusted cooperatives' endorsements. Each cooperative supplies a fixed credit budget. The ledger allocates all agents' limits jointly as flows: an endorsement splits capacity instead of copying it, and cycles add no source credit. If only C credits cross from trusted roots into an attacker's cluster, all its aliases together get at most C. Raising that limit requires a cooperative to commit more scarce credit. Honest root budgets are essential; bribed cooperatives can still back attackers.
